articleTitle: A Novel Source-Grid-Load-Storage Integrated Cooperative System
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: With the rapid development of renewable energy technologies, the proportion of renewables in the power system is increasing. The traditional grid dispatch mode of "source follows load" is not applicable to the new power system. This paper proposes a source-grid-load-storage model and constructs a collaborative system that integrates source, grid, load, and storage. Through a variety of optimization methods, system tools, and information interaction methods, this system can fully leverage the adjustability of the power generation side and the load side, ensuring an accurate match between the supply sides and demand sides. Additionally, it can ensure the safe and stable operation of the power system, achieve optimal resource allocation, and enhance the consumption capacity of clean energy.

articleTitle: Wind Farm Frequency Support Strategy Considering Adjustable Capacity
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: With the decreasing proportion of synchronous generators, the inertia and frequency control ability of high-proportion renewable energy power system have been significantly reduced, requiring the renewable generation to provide enough active power support during grid emergency. In this work, we propose a novel wind farm frequency support strategy to take full advantage of the adjustable capacity of the primary wind energy. Firstly, the nonlinear state space model of the wind turbine is linearized based on the Koopman Operator. Then the model predictive control algorithm is used to optimize the frequency regulation strategy considering wind speed. Finally, the method is verified in the single wind farm and multi-wind farm model. The method not only realizes the active frequency support of the wind farm, but also makes full use of the influence of the wind power on the adjustable capacity of the wind turbines.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Microgrid Based on Multi-objective Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Safety, stability and efficiency, flexible energy flow, and both economic and environmental benefits are the basis for the low-carbon economic operation of the microgrid. However, with the multi-type distributed power sources and flexible loads of multi-stakeholders connected to the microgrid, the environmental protection and economic dispatch model of the microgrid is established considering the operation cost and environmental cost, and the multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MPSO) algorithm is used to solve the optimization model. The effectiveness of the model is verified by Matlab simulation and algorithm comparison, which provides a theoretical basis for the formulation of optimal scheduling strategy for microgrid.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Visualization System of Sustainable Energy Hosting Capacity of the County-wide Distribution Network Based on Safety Constraints
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: With the increasing installed capacity of new energy power generation, the electricity generated by photovoltaic or wind energy in some regions has not been able to be input to the grid, resulting in "wind abandonment" and "photovoltaic energy abandonment". Wind farms are often located in remote areas where electricity is expensive to delivery. Besides, wind power is highly volatile. Sustainable energy generation exceeds limited grid load, causing the abandonment of new energy. In the first three quarters of 2022, the rate of photovoltaic energy abandonment in Tibet is as high as 19.5%, and that in Qinghai is 10.1%. The contradiction between the new installed capacity using new energy and the original grid system structure gradually arose. For an administrative region, due to professional industries and data limitations, its local functional departments cannot be intuitively informed of the real-time consumption capacity of the distribution network in the region. Based on the evaluation and visualization system of sustainable energy penetration rate of the whole county based on safety constraints, this paper conducts systematic analysis and research on the above issues, analyzes the maximum carrying capacity under the premise of safe and stable operation of the distribution network, and presents the results visually.

articleTitle: Reducing Lead Iodide Leaching in Perovskite Solar Cells with a Chelating Bioplastic Layer
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Perovskite solar cells have reached efficiencies ~10% more effective than their silicon counterparts. However, the methylammonium lead iodide compound in perovskite raises concerns regarding potential environmental lead leaching. This paper investigates a novel solution by testing a bioplastic layer bonded to natural chelators derived from kelp, cilantro, chlorella, and spirulina against the chemical chelator, tetrasodium EDTA, on a damaged perovskite solar cell’s production of lead. The layers’ efficacies were determined by testing if they affected the cell’s electrical output and measuring the quantity of lead they trapped. The spirulina chelator performed the best, reducing lead production by 95.31%. The next most efficient was cilantro by 90.64%, tetrasodium by 84.38%, kelp by 74.6%, and chlorella by 64%. Additionally, the paper investigates anti-reflective properties of corn and lotus leaf surface structures imprinted on the bioplastic layer which resulted in a 16.22% and 23.9% efficiency amelioration respectively.

articleTitle: Multi-module Input Series Output Parallel DC/DC Converter Study of Control Strategis
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Multi module input series output parallel (ISOP) DC/DC converters can be used in various applications. In order to ensure the normal operation of the entire system, it is necessary to equalize the input voltage and current between various modules. In this paper, a local information-based input voltage droop equalization control strategy is proposed for ISOP-based DC/DC converter systems. This control strategy has a fast dynamic response, achieves modular operation, high redundancy and improves the reliability of the system. A stability analysis was then performed on the control strategy and its effectiveness and feasibility were verified through simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Research on Evaluation System of Modern Power Supply Service System
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of science and technology, the reform of power system has entered the deep water zone, the environment of electricity sales market is complex and changeable, the reform of electricity price policy and the development of new energy power have promoted profound changes in the whole chain of marketing business, and the quality of power supply service has become an important consideration indicator. Through consulting information and field research, this paper summarizes a set of evaluation methods for modern power supply service system by combining fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method and analytic hierarchy process, which is helpful to the self-improvement and benign development of power supply service

articleTitle: Data Architecture of Source-Grid-Load-Storage Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: With the rapid development of smart-grid, it is increasing for the proportion of new energy in the power system. The emergence of dispatchable resources such as distributed energy storage and flexible load has led to the increasing scale of power grid data and the diversification of data types. The traditional power system dispatching method has gradually exposed some problems, such as inconsistent data transmission protocols, inconsistent business data and insufficient detection of abnormal data in the power grid. In order to cope with the problems of inconsistent power grid business data and insufficient data processing, this article proposes a data architecture of source-grid-load-storage integrated collaborative system, which makes full use of data information to improve data standardization, enhance data transmission capabilities, and improve data processing capabilities to ensure the efficient operation of the power system.

articleTitle: Protection Strategy of Sub-/Super-synchronous in Power Systems with High-Penetration Wind Power
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Sub-/super-synchronous oscillations caused by wind turbines have emerged as one of the primary challenges impeding the widespread utilization of wind power. This paper proposes a protective strategy to address the issue of sub-/super- synchronous oscillations in wind power systems and prevent potential global stability problems in the power grid. Firstly, wind turbine impedance models are constructed using wide-area measurement data. The oscillation source is identified by utilizing the impedance characteristics of wind turbines, and the sub-/super-synchronous current is used to analyze the stability of oscillations. Based on the oscillation source identification and stability analysis results, a protection strategy is developed to enable emergency control of Sub-/super-synchronous oscillations for wind power systems. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed protection strategy is verified.

articleTitle: Generation of synthetic hot water demand profiles with dynamic Markov chains models for end-user-friendly demand response
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Demand response (DR) programmes have been shown to cost-effectively support the safe operation of the electric grid where a significant portion of the energy is generated from renewable sources. These programmes have been implemented via direct or indirect control of the end-user electrical loads. While financial incentives have shown to generate interest in the industrial and the commercial end-user to participate in the programme, this alone fails to entice residential end-users to voluntarily participate in DR programmes. To generate interest in the residential sector, a DR with a low impact on user comfort is needed. When electrical water heaters are targeted for a direct DR scheme, the user comfort is measured by the water temperature of the hot water when needed. To assess this impact without the need to implement costly real-time measurements, a generalised hot water demand that could capture the characteristics of hot water consumption is required. In this paper, multidimensional dynamic Markov chain models are used to generate synthetic hot water demand profiles that take into consideration the stochastic nature of water demand over time without neglecting additional factors that would influence the water demand profile. The dynamic models developed in this study have the propensity to provide generalised hot water demand profiles that consider seasonal and temperature influences in the model’s development. Although the seasonal model performs slightly better than the temperature-based model, both approaches were able to capture the underlying variables determining the hot water demand for domestic electrical water heaters.

articleTitle: Multi-source Joint Optimal Scheduling of Wind-PV-thermal-storage with Frequency Modulation Capability of Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: As renewable energy sources are increasingly connected to the grid, its fluctuating and intermittent nature has brought difficulties and challenges to peak and frequency modulation of the grid. Accordingly, based on the state of charge (SoC) partition of electrochemical energy storage, the SoC-based energy storage peak and frequency modulation work area zoning method is proposed. On this basis, with the minimum variance of net load as the upper optimization goal and the minimum operating cost of the power grid as the lower optimization goal, a two-layer optimal dispatching model is established. Finally, the IEEE-39 system is selected as an example system for analysis, and the results verify the validity and feasibility of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Impact of Load Models on Elevated Neutral-to-Earth Voltage (NEV) in Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: By uniformly grounding the distribution system and the customer's electrical system, neutral-to-earth voltage (NEV) can be moved from the distribution system to grounded objects in a building, like metal water pipes. The customer wiring may also be another possible cause of NEV. Furthermore, NEV is induced by load, leakage, and fault currents flowing through neutral or grounding connections. While ground rods and metallic water lines can channel leakage currents to the earth, every electrical system is subject to voltage-to-earth. Metallic structures connected to neutral or grounding systems will also be at the same NEV. The NEV/stray voltage generally occurs at low voltages and currents, so it is often undetectable. However, when people begin to experience shocks, it becomes a safety issue that, if not addressed, may have a severe impact. Using a backwards/forward sweep approach, this paper examines the effects of various factors on the neutral-to-earth voltage (NEV). An IEEE 13-bus distribution network demonstrates the proposed approach to evaluating NEVs. The results of the study are presented and analyzed. Matlab/Simulink software is used for all simulations.

articleTitle: An Integrated Demand Response-Based Energy Management Strategy for Integrated Energy System Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Integrated demand response represents an effective approach for enhancing energy utilization efficiency while achieving optimal functioning of both supply and demand sides of integrated energy systems. Accounting for the independent response capability of demand users and the inherent uncertainty within the system, an energy management framework is presented based on an enhanced deep reinforcement learning algorithm in this paper. This framework aims to optimize the interaction between the supply and demand sides of integrated energy systems to minimize operational costs. Firstly, an integrated demand response model is introduced, which considers the intricate attributes of multi-energy users and their coupling characteristics with each other. Subsequently, an optimization model is proposed based on an improved deep reinforcement learning algorithm, specifically devised to tackle the challenges posed by system uncertainty. Case simulations show that the proposed method can adapt to the uncertainty of the system and is effective in reducing the energy cost compared to that without the integrated demand response.

articleTitle: Research on Power Line Identification Based on 4D Millimeter Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Power lines threaten the safety of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) flying at low altitude, and accurately recognizing the presence of power lines in the airspace is the key to solve the problem. Based on 4D millimeter wave radar, a power line recognition method is proposed. Through the constant false alarm rate radar signal processing algorithm, the signal threshold is produced, the target echo signal is extracted, the point cloud created from the target signal is fused with multiple frames to enhance the density of the target point cloud, and the scattered points are aggregated into clusters using the DBSCAN clustering algorithm; 11-dimensional feature vectors containing the reflective cross-sectional area (RCS) features are extracted from the clusters to form the dataset, and the optimal parameters are obtained using the Support Vector Machine Classifier with grid searching and cross-validation to identify power lines. The experimental results show that the accuracy of the method based on 4D millimeter-wave radar can reach 98.5%, which can realize the effective recognition of power lines, and the selection of RCS feature vectors can improve the recognition effect.

articleTitle: Research on Spot Market Clearing Method of Electric Energy Storage based on Quantity Declaration Mode
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: To make full use of the flexible regulation characteristics of electric energy storage and solve the problem of insufficient use of electric energy storage under traditional self-scheduling mode, a spot market clearing method of electric energy storage based on electricity declaration mode was proposed. The costs of electric storage are closely related to times and the quantity of charge and discharge. Thus, the energy declaration mode of electric energy storage is proposed based on the operating cost characteristics of electric energy storage. Under this declaration mode, the price of electric energy storage declaration is different from the price under the self-scheduling mode. Market operating institutions construct spot market clearing model, and the charge and discharge times and amount of electric storage are determined by centralized clearing. To verify the effectiveness of the method we proposed, an example was constructed based on the actual data of a provincial power grid. The example results show that the proposed method can reduce the power purchase cost of the grid by nearly 1%, under the same operating cost of electric storage.

articleTitle: Unit Commitment Strategy Based on Multi Energy Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: In order to promote the absorption of wind and photovoltaic power generation, this paper proposes a two-stage constraint handling method for the multi-energy unit commitment problem. In the first stage, constraints such as minimum startup and shutdown times, unit output, and power balance are processed. In the second stage, handling equality constraints such as energy storage capacity and total shiftable load. The coupling of these two stages enables quick and effective seek the optimal startup and shutdown solution, minimizing the operating cost of the system. A case involving 10 thermal power units, wind farms, and a photovoltaic plant was used to test the performance of the proposed method. The results show that the proposed method can efficiently obtain a better unit commitment solution and improve the system economy.

articleTitle: Optimal Schedule Strategy for Peak Shaving Based on the Coordinated Operation of Flexible Resources in Multi-Energy Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: To fully exploit the peak shaving potential of the multi-energy complementary system in a collaborative manner between energy supply and demand, this paper proposes an economic dispatch method for a multi-energy microgrid system that integrates demand response with heat pump technology. The introduction of natural gas heat pumps on the supply side enables energy substitution through multi-energy complementarity, effectively reducing the operating load of peak electricity demand from air conditioning equipment. On the demand side, the electricity price demand response is considered, incorporating user electricity satisfaction into the demand response model to optimize power demand based on user electricity consumption experience, achieving peak load shaving and off-peak load filling. The objective of the optimization is to minimize system operating costs, taking into account energy balance and demand response constraints, and solving the optimization problem using the CPLEX software. The case study demonstrates that the collaborative peak shaving between energy supply and demand can effectively reduce peak electricity demand, leading to improved economic efficiency of the system.

articleTitle: Multi-objective optimal dispatch with electricity and heat energy
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: The power generation of wind power and photovoltaic power are increasing year by year, but their intermittent and fluctuating characteristics increase difficulty in power system dispatch. The combined heat and power unit leads to the wind power and photovoltaic power curtailment due to its heat-determined power characteristic. Combined with thermal energy storage and electric boiler, the combined heat and power unit can decouple the heat-determined power constraint and improve the flexibility. In addition, this paper also adds an energy storage power station to research the possibility of further consumption of wind power and photovoltaic power. The NSGA-II multi-objective algorithm with an improved constraint handling method and decision method which increase wind power and photovoltaic power consumption and convergence speed is presented. The simulation result of the fully dominated Pareto solution set of the modified 10-unit system verifies the effectiveness and superiority of the improved algorithm.

Author Keywords: wind power and photovoltaic power consumption

articleTitle: Integrating Battery Energy Storage Systems in Hot Desert Regions
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: The increasing utilization of solar renewable energy sources in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) regions, including countries such as Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar, highlights the pressing need for Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) to ensure grid stability BESS plays a crucial role in storing excess energy generated during peak generation and supplying it during periods of low generation or high demand. However, integrating BESS in hot desert regions presents unique challenges due to the extreme environmental conditions prevalent in these areas. High ambient temperatures, dust and sandstorms, and intense solar radiation intensity pose obstacles that must be addressed to maximize the effectiveness of BESS deployment. This study aims to identify these obstacles and propose effective solutions for the integration of BESS in hot desert regions. The environmental challenges are analyzed in-depth, considering the impact of high ambient temperatures on battery performance, the accumulation of dust and sand on system components, and the effects of intense solar radiation on system efficiency. By addressing the challenges associated with integrating BESS in hot desert regions, this study contributes to the broader goal of driving sustainable energy solutions in Qatar and the GCC region.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Transformer Substations Based on EWM-GRA
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: As substations have an extremely important role in the power system, it is of great significance to construct a scientific comprehensive evaluation system for substations. Firstly, we construct the substation evaluation system model containing social indicators, safety indicators, economic indicators and energy efficiency indicators, and then determine the indicator weights based on the Entropy Weight Method, and simulate and analyse the actual substation, and introduce the Grey Relational Analysis to rank the comprehensive level of the substation, and the results show that the comprehensive evaluation indicators and model can reflect the comprehensive level of the substation.

articleTitle: Research on Capacitor Aging Behavior and Prediction of Remaining Service Life
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: The AC filter capacitor is an important equipment of DC transmission projects, its safe and reliable operation is a key issue. The existing research lacks a comprehensive life assessment method for the aging stage of capacitors. For this reason, this paper investigates two groups of capacitors with different operating years, and obtains the change law of key aging characteristic quantities during the operation of capacitors by testing and analyzing the insulation performance and durability performance of the body capacitors and their internal materials after dissection; compares multiple characteristic quantities in the time domain, and summarizes the aging mechanism of capacitors; Based on the aging mechanism, a multidimensional assessment method of equipment life state for operation and maintenance is proposed, which provides some reference for predictive maintenance strategy.

articleTitle: An Integrated Optical Method of PV-ESS-CHG V2G Station Based on PSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: In this paper, the basic structure of the optical storage and charging integrated charging station and the distribution control of energy in the system are discussed, and the capacity allocation model of the optical storage and charging system is established by considering the economic return of the charging station and the impact on the grid as the optimization objective, and the optimization solution is combined with the particle swarm optimization algorithm, which can support the planning and construction of the optical storage and charging integrated charging station.

articleTitle: Reactive Power Optimization of Renewable Energy Base Considering Reactive Power Adjustment Capacity of Grid-forming Energy Storage Station
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: In the renewable energy base without synchronous power support, it is difficult to meet the demand of voltage level and dynamic reactive power margin by using conventional reactive power regulation, while the grid-forming battery energy storage station (BESS) has the grid support capability similar to synchronous generator and can participate in the reactive power optimization of the new energy base as a high-quality regulating resource. This paper investigates the reactive power regulation capability of grid-forming BESS based on its control principle and grid-connected characteristics, and proposes a reactive power optimization strategy for renewable energy base, which can dynamically adjust the upper limit of reactive power regulation capacity of BESS according to the change of voltage level and BESS operation status. On this basis, a multi-objective reactive power optimization model considering the operational constraints of grid-forming BESS is constructed, and the effectiveness of the proposed model is verified based on the calculation cases.

articleTitle: Short-term Wind Load Prediction Considering Coupling Characteristics of Multi-energy Complementary System
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: In recent years, the rapid development of renewable energy has been the driving force behind the gradual transformation of the energy industry. The integrated energy system (IES) has become an important method of energy use for energy transformation, linking various energy sources more closely to improve energy use efficiency. Accurate energy forecasting is important for dispatching and operating IES in an economic and optimal way. In this paper, a method for predicting the power load and the wind speed of the integrated power system is proposed on the basis of the EMD-GRU model. First, the original data is decomposed by empirical mode decomposition, and then the candidate features are selected by Pearson correlation coefficient to generate a feature subset. Then, the modal components obtained after the decomposition are predicted separately and superimposed to obtain the final prediction result. Finally, the method has good prediction accuracy through comparative analysis, and the model is verified using data from a specific area.

Author Keywords: wind speed and Electricity Load Forecasting

articleTitle: The Research on Wind turbine blade fatigue test method
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: An important method for determining the fatigue life of a wind turbine blade is wind turbine blade fatigue testing. With a focus on the excitation mode, the relationship between excitation amplitude and vibration frequency, and the vibration principle, this study investigates the issues that arise during the wind turbine blade fatigue test. Then, it suggests practical solutions that could be applied to actual operations.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Optimal Scheduling Model for Electric Vehicle Charging Considering Distribution Network Operation
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: In this study, a sparrow search algorithm is used to establish a multi-objective optimization model for minimizing peak-to-valley load difference and network loss in distribution networks to achieve optimal scheduling of EV charging behavior. The validity and correctness of the method is verified by IEEE-33 nodes, and comparative analysis with the traditional disordered charging scenario reveals that the EV charging strategy using the intelligent optimization algorithm is able to significantly mitigate the grid load fluctuation, reduce the voltage excursion, and decrease the active network loss, which improves the security and economy of the power system operation.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of User-side Integrated Energy System Containing Biomass CHP
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Under the background of the "Double Carbon Targets", biomass energy, as an environmentally friendly renewable energy source, plays an important role in the process of carbon emission reduction. China's rural areas are rich in biomass energy resources, but the overall utilization rate is low. In view of the above problems, this paper constructs an optimal operating model of user-side integrated energy system (USIES) containing biomass CHP, using biomass CHP units to improve biomass energy utilization and reduce the overall energy cost of the system; ground source heat pump (GSHP) is introduced as clean heating equipment to reduce system carbon emissions by reducing coal consumption for traditional coal-fired heating, consuming the surplus of wind power in the time of high wind power generation and assuming the task of night-time heating; By decoupling the system's electricity and heat through electric and thermal energy storage, the impact on the system's operating efficiency caused by the fixed ratio of electricity and heat of the CHP unit is weakened, thus increasing the energy utilization rate of wind power and biomass CHP. The simulation example shows that the optimal operation model constructed in this paper can reduce carbon emissions while ensuring the economy of system operation, and provide reference for the future utilization of biomass energy and the optimal operation of integrated energy system.

articleTitle: Reward Mechanism Design for Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Microgrid Energy Management
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), with its data-driven nature and model-free advantage, has attracted great interest in the field of microgrid energy management system. The choice of reward mechanism plays a crucial role in the performance and effectiveness of DRL-based microgrid energy management. This paper aims to investigate the reward mechanism design by comparing the performances of DRL-based microgrid energy management under two different reward mechanisms, namely, cliff walking pattern and Leduc poker pattern. The reward mechanism incorporates auxiliary rewards alongside the primary reward to harmonize diverse objectives. Using a real microgrid dataset, the performance of DRL agents under different reward mechanisms are compared. The experimental results demonstrate that different reward mechanisms have a significant impact on the convergence speed and generalization ability of trained microgrid energy management policy.

articleTitle: Study of overhead grounding wire and preformed armor rods port based on multi-physical field coupling
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Because of the sharply rose temperature, only limited physical quantities can be obtained in the short-time impact experiment of overhead grounding wire and preformed armor rods port. Therefore, in order to further analyze various physical quantities in the process of short-circuit current passing through, a three-dimensional finite element simulation model of multi-physical field that electromagnetic, thermal-solid was established in this paper, and the current density distribution, transient temperature distribution and Von Mises stress distribution were calculated.

articleTitle: Power Shaping Control of Single-Phase Grid-Connected Converter Based on Brayton-Moser Model
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: To enhance the dynamic characteristics of single-phase grid-connected converters and analyze system stability, this paper employs the hybrid potential function theory to model the single-phase grid-connected converter and conduct stability domain analysis, obtaining quantitative criteria for large-signal disturbance stability. Drawing inspiration from the passive control damping injection concept, the power shaping controller is designed by combining the system's Mixed Potential Function (MPF) and Brayton-Moser (BM) model. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed criterion facilitates easy assessment and analysis of system stability. When the system experiences large-signal disturbances, if the parameters satisfy the criterion, the output voltage returns to its rated value swiftly. Furthermore, the proposed power shaping control strategy outperforms the traditional PI control strategy, providing better dynamic and steady-state performances for the converter under large-signal disturbance condition.

articleTitle: Large-Scale Renewable Energy Power Aggregation Modeling Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: In this paper, the mechanism and aggregation method of wind and solar power participating in the system frequency process are clarified through the studies of inertia and frequency modulation modelling and frequency support capability aggregation. Firstly, based on the historical wind power and PV output data, a mathematical model describing the output characteristics of wind power and PV at the second and minute scales is established. Secondly, the relationship between the renewable energy hourly average frequency support capability and minute and second scale frequency support characteristics is analyzed. Finally, different hourly equivalent methods such as hourly average frequency support capacity (FSC) and hourly minimum FSC are compared and analyzed, and the equivalent frequency support capacity applicable to hourly planning and operation is studied. Results verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis of the relationship between renewable energy outputs and frequency response capability and the proposed aggregation model.

Author Keywords: output model of wind and solar

articleTitle: Evolution Characteristics of Dielectric Constant and Resistivity of Different Oil-impregnated Paperboard with Increasing Aging Time
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: As the key apparatus of HVDC transmission, converter transformers have a high insulation failure rate. Under the actual operating conditions of UHV converter transformers, the internal oil-impregnated paper material might gradually age due to the combined action of multiple physics such as large temperature gradient and electric field. However, there are few studies on the aging characteristics of key insulation parameters of KI50X, HI50X and S4 transformer oil-impregnated paperboard which are widely used. This paper studied the dielectric constant and material resistance characteristics of three transformer oil-impregnated paperboard after aging at a high temperature of 90°C for 1 day, 7 days, 21 days, 28 days and 35 days. And we obtained the evolution law of the dielectric constant and resistance characteristics of the three oil-impregnated paperboards under long-term operating conditions, and compared the three transformer oils from different parameter perspectives, which could provide a basis and reference for the selection of insulating oils for converter transformers.

articleTitle: Research on Control Parameters Analysis and Oscillation Suppression Strategy of Permanent Magnetic Synchronous Generator Based on Grid-Forming Control
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: With the increase of permeability of renewable energy and power electronic equipment, the inertia and damping parameters of the direct-drive wind turbine based on grid-forming control have a large impact on the system stability, and the system oscillation will be triggered when the parameters are not set properly. In this paper, the problem is addressed by establishing the small-signal model of two permanent magnetic synchronous generators connected to the grid in detail, analyzing the influence of the active control parameters on the system stability through the root locus of the dominant characteristic root, and proposing the adaptive control of damping and inertia to suppress the system oscillations. Finally, a real-time simulation platform for grid-connected wind turbine systems was built, and the experimental results verifies the correctness of the small-signal model for stability analysis of grid-forming wind turbines established in this paper.

articleTitle: Function Specifications of Source-Grid-Load-Storage Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: In response to the challenges of high integration difficulty and poor data security in current collaborative control, this paper proposes a functional architecture control platform based on source-grid-load-storage integrated collaborative control. Through the application of platform layer, application layer, and functional layer, it can achieve the collaborative operation and optimized control of various resources, and more effectively manage and dispatch energy.

articleTitle: Effect of Wave Conditions on Offshore Floating Photovoltaic Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: The offshore floating photovoltaic power generation system is an effective method to solve the contradiction between land photovoltaic development and land resources. Compared to land-based photovoltaic power generation systems, the impact of waves on the performance of floating photovoltaic power generation cannot be ignored. In this paper, double-diode modeling is used to model the photovoltaic cell; then, the influence of waves on the inclination angle of photovoltaic panels is analyzed, taking into account the effects of temperature and wind speed; finally, the power generation performance of photovoltaic panels under different sea conditions is simulated and analyzed, taking the actual sea conditions in Bohai Bay as an example. The experimental results show that compared with land photovoltaic power generation systems, the output power of offshore floating photovoltaic power generation systems has increased by 4.8% - 13.04%.

articleTitle: Research on Voltage Source and Current Source Control of Three-phase Grid-connected Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: The grid-connected converter is the main interface between distributed generation and grid. The research can ensure its stable operation under different grid conditions, and it is crucial to promote the development of renewable energy. The control of grid-connected converter can be divided into voltage source control (VSC) and current source control (CSC). In this paper, the influence of grid impedance on converter’s stability is analyzed in both VSC and CSC controls, and a switching control strategy is also proposed to meet the need of switching between different controls. On the basis of theory analysis, the simulations based on Simulink have been conducted, and the results show that the proposed switching control strategy can achieve smooth switching between different controls without obvious surge current.

articleTitle: Day-ahead Scheduling for Improving the Transfer Capability Utilization Rate of Transmission Interface with Battery Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Investigating the transfer capability utilization rate of transmission interface flow is one of the important steps for formulating the day-ahead renewable power generation schedule. However, restrained by transmission limitations and curtailments, the dispatch-down of renewable energy has already become a prominent problem that declines the utilization rate of transmission interfaces. In this paper, a day-ahead scheduling model considering the flexibility of battery energy storage (BES) is proposed. Transmission interface constraints are introduced to limit the magnitude and direction of the power flow across the specific interface. By optimizing the proposed model, the charging and discharging schedule of BES units is obtained to regulate the output of wind and thermal units and fully utilize the transfer capability of the interface. Moreover, compared with different scenarios of load fluctuation, the positive effect of BES on a flexible day-ahead scheduling is analyzed. Comprehensive case studies on the modified IEEE 30-bus system validate that the BES is effective to improve the utilization rate of transmission interfaces without wind curtailments.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of a Battery-Supercapacitor Hybrid Energy Storage System (HESS) for Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Fossil fuels have been used as a source of electrical energy since the development and advancements of electrical grids, with AC always being the preferred form of power. As time progressed, DC was steadily advancing to catch up with AC with various developments of HVDC networks. The invention of DC microgrids gave new light to the future of DC power utilization. Various energy management systems have since been developed to optimize DC power. One of the systems of note is the Battery-supercapacitor Hybrid Energy Storage System (HESS). Every system must be developed, modeled, and analyzed to have a technical grasp of how the system will operate under diverse loading and conditions if it is to be operated at its optimal level. This paper serves the purpose of a review on the subject matter and modeling that have undergone using MATLAB/Simulink software. Simulations are run for changes in loading and system conditions. Observation is then made on the system's components' response concerning system major parameters such as the voltage, current, power, and states of charge (SoC). After the results are obtained, they are analyzed, and conclusions and recommendations are made.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of Integrated Energy System with Coupled Energy Storage Based on Stackelberg Game
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Understanding the interaction strategy between multiple energy agents is the main challenge in optimizing the operation of integrated energy system. This paper proposes an optimal operation strategy of integrated energy system with coupled energy storage based on Stackelberg game. The interactive strategy corresponding to the optimal benefits of multiple agents is obtained in the Stackelberg leader-follower framework. The integrated energy operator acts as the leader, formulating the pricing strategy based on users' demands, while the energy user act as the follower and determine their energy consumption based on the prices set by the operator. The case study results indicate that the proposed optimization model successfully achieves the "source-load-storage" synergistic optimization, ultimately leading to a reduction in the overall cost of the system, while simultaneously preserving customer satisfaction. By balancing the fluctuation of electric and heat loads, energy storage modules have the potential to considerably improve the overall economy and safety of system operations.

articleTitle: Study of 18650 LiFePO4 Lithium-Ion Battery Cells for Stationary and EV Applications: Performance, Reliability, and Safety
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: The increasing demand for energy storage in both stationary and electric vehicle (EV) applications necessitates a thorough evaluation of the performance, reliability, and safety of lithium-ion battery cells. Performance analysis involves investigating key parameters such as capacity, energy efficiency, and cycle life. Reliability assessment encompasses long-term cycling tests, accelerated aging experiments, and capacity retention analysis to determine the cells' durability under varying operating conditions. Safety evaluation involves analyzing thermal stability and determining the battery's state of health. This study presents a comprehensive assessment of 18650 LiFePO4 (LFP) lithium-ion battery cells for stationary and EV applications. The cells were aged at different temperatures, states of charge (SOC), and depths of discharge (DOD) to determine the extent of capacity fade and degradation. The results showed that the DOD and charging protocol during aging play a crucial role in the performance of the cells. Cells with lower DOD exhibited reduced capacity loss and higher state of health (SOH). Furthermore, the study indicates that cells stored in a fully discharged state at room temperature exhibit better capacity retention and higher SOH compared to cells stored at higher temperatures. The heat generation rate of all tested cells was relatively low, indicating the good thermal stability of the cells, ensuring their safety and performance.

articleTitle: Induction Motor Fault Identification using Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Different induction motor applications have subjected this machine to different conditions that will affect its effective operation. Various types of faults are caused by the environment in which induction motors are installed, which eventually affect the entire operation of the industrial plant, these machines operate. This study aims to develop a more effective method for identifying and classifying faults in three-phase induction motors using Support Vector Machines. The method of Artificial Intelligence (AI), which incorporates the Support Vector Machines (SVM) algorithm, is used to classify nine conditions of fault in induction motors, namely the unbalanced supply voltages, over-voltage, under-voltage, blocked rotor, line-to-line short circuit, line-to-earth short circuit, single phasing, mechanical overload, and a healthy motor. A SIMULINK simulation of an induction motor will be created to simulate the faults independently, and the results will be trained to the SVM model. Using an Orange tool, the SVM method was used in conjunction with the one-versus-all multiclass approach and the Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel.

articleTitle: Service Life Prediction Method of Transformer in Prefabricated Substation Based on BOA-BP Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: The operation status of transformers should be crucial for ensuring the normal operation of prefabricated intelligent substations, and accurate assessment and prediction of transformer service life is key to ensuring their safety and stability. This paper proposed a method for predicting transformer service life based on Bayesian optimization and BP neural network. This method extracted effective features from transformer operational data and evaluates its status and remaining service life through a health indicator. The effectiveness of this method was verified on data from a certain transformer, providing scientific guidance for the maintenance work of prefabricated intelligent substations.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Flat-chip Solid Oxide Fuel Cells with Discrete Interconnector Designs
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Flat-chip solid oxide fuel cells (FCSOFCs) possess advantages in rapid start-up and thermal shock resistance. However, a significant performance discrepancy remains between single cell and stack. In this study, a 3D multi-physics model for the one-cell stack is developed based on the realistic structure and verified through experiments. For the first time, the impact of integrating the interconnectors on FCSOFC stack performance is investigated. Compared to the conventional parallel interconnector design, a suitable discrete design mitigates oxygen starvation and promotes a more uniform temperature distribution, effectively enhancing stack performance. As a result, the output power can be improved by up to 21.4%. The model presented in this study offers insightful guidance for the design of FCSOFC stacks.

articleTitle: Research on Interturn Short Circuit Fault Diagnosis of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator Based on CWGAN-GP and CNN-TSA-GRU
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the number of fault samples of permanent magnet synchronous motor is too small and unbalanced in the actual work process, a fault diagnosis method of permanent magnet synchronous motor based on conditional Wasserstein Generative adversarial network (CWGAN-GP) and Convolutional neural network (CNN) is proposed. Firstly, the CWGAN-GP Generative adversarial network is constructed by combining the conditional Generative adversarial network (CGAN) and the gradient penalty Wasserstein distance based Generative adversarial network (WGAN-GP); Then, a small number of fault data samples are input into CWGAN-GP to obtain high-quality samples similar to the original samples. When the network reaches Nash equilibrium, the generated samples will be mixed with the original samples to generate a new sample set; The improved temporal self attention mechanism is used to assign weights to the data, and Convolutional neural network CNN is used to extract spatial features, weaken redundant feature information, and retain target features; Finally, the gating loop unit GRU is used to extract the temporal features of the sample data, enabling the network to learn more fully and improving model robustness. Finally, the new sample set is input into the Convolutional neural network to learn the sample features for fault diagnosis. The experimental results show that the diagnostic method proposed in this article has an accuracy of over 98.9%, which is higher than other diagnostic methods, effectively improving diagnostic accuracy and enhancing its generalization ability.

articleTitle: Intelligent Building Indoor Temperature Control Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: The sustainable development and intelligent construction of building energy systems have become an inevitable trend of global energy development. The indoor temperature control has gradually played an important role in promoting energy saving and consumption reduction of buildings in the whole society. According to the physical characteristics of the wall, this paper constructs a RC network thermodynamic model of the building system. Taking the room temperature comfort and economy as the optimization goals, a deep reinforcement learning algorithm, namely, deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG), is employed to determine the optimal heating and cooling strategies for temperature control devices under different weather conditions. By comparing the temperature variations, energy consumption, and electricity costs, it is observed that DDPG outperforms deep Q-network (DQN) significantly. Furthermore, cross-validation using the Gurobi Optimizer demonstrates that in both summer and winter seasons, where energy consumption accounts for 75% of the total, the performance of the deep reinforcement learning algorithm is equal to or even surpasses Gurobi Optimizer. Moreover, compared with the solver's performance, DDPG's total energy consumption in summer and winter is reduced by 4%. This demonstrates that deep reinforcement learning algorithms such as DDPG exhibit high generalization capability and practicality in complex system control and scheduling problems.

articleTitle: Study on the fault diagnosis of rolling bearings based on the CNN-BiLSTM method
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Study on the fault diagnosis of motor rolling bearings is particularly important to the use and safety management of bearings and the motor system. Therefore, a fault diagnosis method for motor rolling bearings based on the CNN-BiLSTM model is proposed in this work. The model uses the convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract features and reduce data dimensions of the input vector to the model, and employs the bi-directional long-short memory network (BiLSTM) to learn the time correlation information of the input time series in the local features, so as to implement the operation state monitoring and fault diagnosis of rolling bearings. The experimental results prove the effectiveness of the model, and its fault diagnosis accuracy of motor rolling bearings reached 98.62%, which can meet the requirements for practical use.

articleTitle: Multi-step short-term wind power prediction based on spatio-temporal graph convolutional networks
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Wind power generation has been developed rapidly in recent years. However, the inherent volatility and intermittency of wind power bring challenges to the stability of the power system, so it is of great significance to improve the accuracy of wind power prediction. In this paper, a wind power prediction model based on spatio-temporal graph convolutional network is proposed. Here, turbines are considered as nodes of a graph with a learnable adjacency matrix that determines the strength of relationships between turbines based on historical wind speed and wind power data, and a self-loop connectivity matrix is added to the adjacency matrix to increase the self-connectivity of each node. In this way, we effectively integrate the spatial dependencies and temporal trends of neighboring turbines. Experiments conducted on a real dataset collected from onshore wind farms in the U.S. show that our proposed model outperforms a previously developed baseline model on the reference dataset.

articleTitle: Research on the Impact of Carbon Emission Reduction Technology on the Cost of Transmission and Transformation Project Based on Hierarchical Analysis Method
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: With the global warming and increasing occurrences of extreme weather events, reducing carbon emissions has become a worldwide focal point. Within the power industry, the transmission and distribution of electricity stand as significant sources of carbon emissions. This paper aims to employ the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to compute indicator weights and determine that grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) technology has the most substantial impact on the cost of transmission and substation engineering. By constructing an assessment framework considering both the decarbonization and economic benefits of grid-connected PV technology, a specific case study is conducted. This study thereby offers a scientific foundation for the sustainable development of the power industry.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Industrial Process and Power Demand Response: A Case Study in Cement
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: The construction of new power system puts forward higher requirements for demand-side management, and it is necessary to further tap the adjustable load resources to stabilize the fluctuation of the power grid. A large number of studies on tapping adjustable resources have been carried out in the fields of industry, transportation, commerce, agriculture, and residents. Among them, the industrial side has concentrated load and large energy consumption, which meets the requirements of interruptible and adjustable power load and has great adjustable potential. At the same time, processes such as craft are closely related to the adjustable potential. Interruptible and adjustable loads should not hinder normal production and operation. Therefore, it is necessary to study the adjustable resources of the industrial side considering the craft and process. In this paper, the research is carried out based on the cement industry in the basic industry. The process is established into a scheduling model through the state task network. The MILP method is used to optimize the total price of all states in the process minus the maximum value of the difference between the use cost of all equipment. The optimal scheduling and adjustable potential changes under different warehouse settings and warehouse material quantities are studied.

articleTitle: Cluster Control Technology of AC and DC Charging and Replacing Facilities for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: The primary focus of this paper is on the modeling of load characteristics, node aggregation and partitioning strategy, and partition-based minimum cost frequency regulation optimization for electric vehicle charging and swapping stations. Regarding the load characteristic modeling for charging and swapping stations, a probabilistic modeling approach was employed. The time distribution of different types of electric vehicle (EV) charging behaviors was estimated using historical statistical data, utilizing methods like moment estimation or maximum likelihood estimation. Subsequently, the daily load variation curve for a specific charging station or EV cluster was computed through the application of Monte Carlo simulation. To achieve a stable and smooth model update for the rolling strategy, specific model updating schemes were designed. For the optimization of the minimum cost frequency regulation, a constrained linear programming problem was constructed based on the results of partitioning. Through the solution of this problem, adjustments for each node at each time moment could be determined, facilitating the formulation of scheduling strategies.

articleTitle: Optimal Distributed Control of Voltage Regulation in Rural Active Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: In this paper, we develop an optimal distributed control model for voltage regulation in rural active distribution networks (RADN) with a high proportion of photovoltaic generation (PV). The developed model considers the branch power flow model and the photovoltaic inverter model of dynamic distribution networks. The primary objective is to minimize bus voltage deviation, reduce fluctuations of PV, and minimize network losses. We leverage the second-order cone relaxation technique to convexify the model. The disadvantages of centralized optimization control, such as high computational complexity and concerns regarding information privacy, could be avoided via the decomposition and coordination principle of the active distribution networks. The developed model highlights the distributed cooperative optimization control framework. To enhance the convergence performance of the algorithm, we propose an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) based on the residual balance principle and relaxation techniques. The effectiveness of the proposed optimal distributed control model is validated through simulations of the IEEE 33 test system installed with PV.

Author Keywords: Accelerated alternating direction method of multipliers

articleTitle: Hierarchical Interactive Mechanism for Flexible Demand Response of Multi-Energy Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: With the development of microgrid technology and demand-side aggregating technologies, a flexible and cost-effective interactive mechanism has become an effective solution for optimizing energy utilization in microgrids and promoting flexible interactions among multiple adjustable resources. This study focuses on multi-energy microgrids as the research object. Firstly, to promote flexible interactions among multiple adjustable resources, a multi-level interactive architecture for multi-energy microgrid systems is established. Secondly, various interactive modes such as demand-side multi-energy coordinated operation and joint demand response are discussed. Based on this, considering the complementary demand between thermal energy and electrical energy within the microgrid, a hierarchical demand response model for microgrids is established. Furthermore, a hierarchical interactive mechanism for responding to the demands of multi-energy microgrids is designed, which effectively reduces the operational costs of microgrids and achieves a win-win situation for multiple parties. Finally, the effectiveness and economic feasibility of the designed mechanism are verified through simulations.

articleTitle: Flexible Transmission Network Expansion Planning Considering Multi-path Deep Peak Regulation and Network Structure Regulation under Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Carbon reduction encounters insufficient power system regulation, flexible planning is vital to deal with uncertainties in enhancing carbon neutral, which needs to consider various flexible resources. In this paper, the multipath deep peak regulation as a generator side flexible resource and network structure regulation as a network side flexible resource is proposed to enhance the power system flexibility. A novel model considering multipath deep peak regulation and network structure regulation under uncertainty is proposed. Static and transient security constraints are satisfied in the model. The proposed method is verified by a real-world test system, the comparison of involving deep peak regulation, the flexible index and the security constraints are presented. The simulation results demonstrate that the method can effectively provide the optimal results.

articleTitle: High Impedance Grounding Fault Protection for Low-resistance Grounding System Based on the Ratio of Phase Active Power Variation
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: The high impedance grounding fault of medium voltage distribution network is always a difficult and hot point in distribution network protection. Aiming at the problem that the traditional zero-sequence current protection is difficult to identify the faulty line due to the small short-circuit current when the single-phase grounding fault with high impedance occurs in the low-resistance grounding system, this paper studies the power frequency variation of the phase active power of the faulty line, and analyzes that the power frequency variation of the faulty phase active power is much larger than that of the nonfaulty phase, while the power frequency variation of the nonfaulty line is similar. Therefore, a distribution network protection scheme based on the power frequency variation of phase active power is proposed. This scheme constructs the three-phase ratio criterion of the power frequency variation of phase active power by using the difference of the power frequency variation of three-phase active power after the fault occurs. Finally, based on PSCAD/EMTDC simulation experiments, it is verified that the proposed algorithm can withstand the faulty resistance of 2000Ω in the low-resistance grounding system.

articleTitle: Human-Tolerance-Oriented Fault Recovery Strategy for Regional Integrated Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: In response to multiple failures arising from extreme disasters, both the electricity and thermal aspects of regional integrated energy systems (RIES) are interdependent during the fault recovery process. In this paper, a fault recovery strategy is proposed to enhance the disaster recovery efficiency of RIES, considering the thermal comfort for individuals to ensure their health across various fault scenarios. Firstly, the thermal inertia model is demonstrated that the thermal load can be spatially and temporally transferred in incremental quantities. Additionally, the heat exchange model is designed to provide a basis for the strategy. Moreover, a dual-objective optimization model is established to simultaneously analyze the economic cost and temperature reduction. The concluding case study validates the effectiveness of the proposed strategy under different fault scenarios.

articleTitle: Research on Big Data Scenario of Power Marketing Service System
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: With the rapid development of big data technology, the field of power marketing service gradually applies big data technology to realize fine management and personalized service. This paper aims to study the construction of big data scenarios in power marketing services and explore their effects. Firstly, the concept, characteristics and development status of power marketing service are introduced. Then, the application scenarios of big data technology in power marketing service system were expounded in detail, including user portrait analysis, personalized recommendation, marketing strategy optimization, customer relationship management, data security and privacy protection. Then, the big data scenarios of power marketing service system were mainly studied, including data collection and analysis and power marketing service scene analysis. Through the steps of data source and collection method, data preprocessing and cleaning, data analysis and mining method, the depth analysis and mining of power user data are realized. In the scenario analysis of the power marketing service system, the user portrait scenario, personalized recommendation scenario, marketing strategy optimization scenario, customer relationship management scenario, data security and privacy protection scenario are studied. Finally, the application effect of the big data scene of the power marketing service system was evaluated, and the optimization suggestions were put forward. The results show that the application of big data technology in power marketing service system can improve service quality, enhance user experience, and provide scientific basis for power enterprises to make decisions.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Evaluation and Optimal Selection of Carbon Reduction Technologies for Power Transmission and Transformation Projects
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: In order to grasp the intrinsic relationship between carbon reduction and cost and benefit of power transmission and transformation projects, the cost-benefit evaluation index system of power transmission and transformation projects is established. Hierarchical analysis is used to determine the weight of each indicator on the cost and benefit, and then entropy weighting method is used to standardize the indicators and correct the weights, so as to establish a more perfect comprehensive evaluation system for power transmission and transformation projects. Based on this system, eight alternative carbon reduction programs are proposed, and the whole life cycle net present value and cash flow of the eight transformation programs are calculated one by one and the comprehensive scoring of the programs is carried out. In the final guideline layer, the highest weighting is given to the technology of "adopting new transformers", and the retrofit based on Program 7 is expected to achieve higher efficiency through lower costs.

articleTitle: Distribution Network Structure Planning Method Including DC Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: As more and more distributed power is connected to the distribution network, the distribution network gradually transitions from the traditional one-way power receiving and distributing to users to the active network of supply and demand interaction. In this paper, a two-layer programming model is proposed for the DC construction of the distribution network, which is used to optimize the allocation of the DC construction of the urban distribution network and achieve the purpose of taking into account the construction effect and construction economy.

articleTitle: Research on Capacity Allocation Optimization and Operational Strategies with Multiple Types of Energy Storage under New Energy Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: High levels of thermal power generation result in significant consumption of fossil energy and environmental pollution. To achieve the dual carbon goals, it is crucial to expedite the advancement of the proportion of new energy generation and establish a power generation structure where new energy serves as the main component, with multiple forms of energy synergistically complementing each other. In response to the uncertainty and randomness of wind and solar power generation, the approach of integrating energy storage into the new power system is employed for capacity configuration optimization and adjustment. This paper constructs a comprehensive energy and power system incorporating photovoltaic, wind power, thermal power, pumped-storage, and electrochemical energy storage. Maximizing profits is set as the objective function, and the optimization problem is solved using the CPLEX solver. Furthermore, a comparison of wind and solar curtailment rates and overall profits is conducted for four different scenarios, ultimately concluding that the multi-type energy storage configuration strategy outperforms the single-type energy storage configuration. This validates the economic feasibility of optimizing the integration of multiple types of energy storage into the new power system.

articleTitle: A Bilateral Electricity Market Settlement Model Considering Unbalanced Fund Handling
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: Aiming at the key issues such as dual track settlement and volume price relationship between the bilateral spot market and the contract market, this paper constructed a dual track electricity market settlement model based on the principle of "day ahead benchmark, real-time quantity difference and contract price difference", consider the unbalanced fund allocation/return mechanism of the responsible parties. On this basis, the market data of a certain province is used for simulation, considering multiple types of units on the generation side and multiple types of users on the load side, and analyzing the volume price relationship of each entity and the causes of unbalanced funds, to provide relevant reference suggestions for the settlement of the bilateral electricity market.

articleTitle: Power Optimization Allocation Method of Direct-Drive Wind Turbines for Mitigating Grid Transient Frequency Dip
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: With the increasing penetration level of wind power, the inertia and frequency regulation ability of the power grid will be significantly reduced. After fault occurrence, the wind turbines enter the low voltage ride-through (LVRT) and implement a post-fault delay active power recovery, causing a short-term large power shortage that may result in a serious frequency dip. This paper proposes a power optimization allocation method for direct-drive wind turbines to mitigate grid frequency dip. Firstly, the power response and energy conversion process of the wind farm (WF) and synchronous generator during the complete LVRT processes are analyzed. It is found that the energy shortage caused by WF during the LVRT recovery process can approximately reflect the frequency dip. Then, taking the wake effect into account, an optimization method is designed in which the objective is to minimize the energy shortage caused by WF during the LVRT recovery process by adjusting the pre-fault steady state power of upstream and downstream wind turbines. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed optimization method is verified in different wind speed scenarios.

articleTitle: An intra-day rolling scheduling optimization method considering the dynamic adjustment of operation reserve
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: In order to ensure the sufficient operation reserve of the power grid during real-time operation and adjust the deviation of operation reserve caused by the deviation of new energy and electricity load prediction in time, an intra-day rolling scheduling optimization method considering the dynamic adjustment of operation reserve was proposed. The operation reserve deviation will be evaluated according to the current generation output of the generation unit and the rolling forecast of new energy and electricity load. Fully considering the impact of positive and negative deviations of operation reserve on power grid operation, the principle of rolling scheduling optimization adjustment with the goal of minimizing the comprehensive power purchase cost is proposed. An intra-day rolling scheduling optimization model considering dynamic adjustment of operational reserve is proposed, which fully considers the change of comprehensive power purchase cost and its adjustment amplitude to the day-ahead generation plan. The scheduling plan will be re-optimized by solving the above optimization model. Finally, a case study based on the actual data of a provincial power grid was constructed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The example results show that the proposed method can avoid the large adjustment of the day-ahead plan by the rolling plan, and reduce the comprehensive power purchase cost by about 1% compared with the traditional method.

articleTitle: Approach of Flexible Load Control Strategy Based on Group Control for PV-ESS-CHG V2G Stations
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: In this paper, in the context of the large-scale application of new energy vehicles, we propose a method of using photovoltaic, energy storage and V2G technologies to solve the power load pressure brought by charging piles to the power grid. This paper firstly constructs the probabilistic models of PV power generation and EV charging pile load, then proposes a day-ahead planning model for solving the thermal unit power generation plan and PV energy storage construction plan, and a real-time planning model for solving the energy storage device deployment scheme and charging pile V2G deployment scheme, and deterministically transforms the chance constraints and arbitrariness constraints therein by using sampling methods. Finally, this paper obtains a comparison of the performance of various aspects of the system before and after the construction of photovoltaic energy storage by solving the IEEE30 node model, proving that the method proposed in this paper is able to effectively reduce the operating cost, improve the stability of the system, and play a role in shaving peaks and filling valleys.

articleTitle: V2G Hierarchical Grouping Control Considering Users’ Behaviour Flexibility
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Renewable Energy and Power Engineering (REPE)
abstract: The widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EV) has increased the burden on the power grid. Employing V2G technology with unified control over the charging and discharging of electric vehicles presents an effective response strategy. Conventional V2G optimization control schemes often suffer from issues such as insufficient control precision, inadequate consideration of user behaviour flexibility, and frequent battery charge-discharge cycles. This paper proposes a charge and discharge priority index based on which a hierarchical grouping control strategy is designed for peak regulation in distribution networks. It ensures user behaviour flexibility and mitigating the need for frequent battery charge-discharge cycles. In the case study, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed control strategy effectively utilizes the EV cluster as a controllable load, reducing peak-valley differences in the distribution network while ensuring user mobility.
